turns.input: *He looks at Jessa Rook, trying to understand what kind of person he has in front of him.*
turns.draft:
Jessa Rook stands in the square not far from Heartstone's entrance, where foot traffic moves at an unhurried midday pace. She is tall and solidly built, dark hair heavily streaked grey, a narrow pale scar cutting across one eyebrow. Her sleeves are rolled above the forearms and a small notebook is tucked into her belt. She carries herself with the easy stillness of someone accustomed to sizing up strangers — her gaze tracks hands, belt pouches, the worn points of luggage and clothing before settling on faces.

She notices the attention. Her expression doesn't shift toward warmth or suspicion — just a level, unhurried appraisal in return, the kind that seems to weigh what sort of trouble might walk through a door before deciding whether to care. There is no hurry in it, no challenge, nothing performative. She simply looks back, waiting to see whether the tall, heavyset man with the first threads of grey in his hair will speak, move on, or stand there studying her a moment longer.
